newsitem.title: JAPAN: GE Capital, Sakura units agree to business tie-up.
newsitem.headline: GE Capital, Sakura units agree to business tie-up.

text.p: Tokyo-based consumer credit firm General Electric Capital Consumer Finance (GECF), a wholly owned unit of GE Capital of the United States, said on Friday it had agreed to a business tie-up with a unit of Sakura Bank Ltd.
GECF and Sakura Finance Service will form a cooperative relationship to jointly develop their customer bases and promote their respective businesses, GECF said in a statement.
GECF's business is centred on the consumer shopping credit and credit card businesses. Its parent company, GE Capital, is a member of the General Electric Co group.
Sakura Finance's core business is collection services on behalf of companies and organisations. The business is conducted through a system of automatic debiting.
GECF said that under the tie-up agreement, Sakura Finance will introduce its customers to GECF, adding that it will introduce some of its own clients to Sakura Finance.
"Through an agreement complementing each other's strengths, the partners aim to have greater opportunities to develop new markets," GECF said.
